endorsements.quote: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), such as those with a cluster and factorial design, can be structured to compare AI-augmented clinical decisions to standard physician judgment and will be crucial in validating the utility of RL and similar AI approaches in clinical practice18.

Looking toward the future, subsequent iterations of RL models should incorporate intuitive visualization tools and transparent decision pathways, enabling physicians to quickly and critically assess AI-driven suggestions rather than accepting them uncritically.

unlisted_practices: Conduct prospective validation, ideally randomized trials, of offline reinforcement learning models before clinical adoption.
Retrain AI models regularly with updated patient data to keep them relevant as guidelines, practices, and populations change.
Conduct cost-effectiveness and cost-utility assessments of AI tools.
Embed explainable AI techniques such as feature attribution, saliency maps, and counterfactual explanations in clinical decision support models.
Foster interdisciplinary collaboration among data scientists, physicians, and administrators to refine AI systems and address bias.
Ensure AI tools comply with privacy and data security regulations when training on sensitive medical records.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective discussing the potential of offline reinforcement learning in cardiovascular disease management and key challenges for implementation and governance.
